source: Sulla S, in un'ora di traffico. Un tipo di circa ventisei anni, cappello floscio con una cordicella al posto del nastro, collo troppo lungo, come se glielo avessero tirato. La gente scende. Il tizio in questione si arrabbia con un vicino. Gli rimprovera di spingerlo ogni volta che passa qualcuno. Tono lamentoso, con pretese di cattiveria. Non appena vede un posto libero, vi si butta. Due ore più tardi lo incontro alla Cour de Rome, davanti alla Gare Saint-Lazare. È con un amico che gli dice: «Dovresti far mettere un bottone in più al soprabito». Gli fa vedere dove (alla sciancratura) e perché.

In the bustling supermarket checkout line, customers lined up in anticipation, their bags heavy and urgent. In front of them, a tall, imposing cash register stood sentinel, its sleek metal surface gleaming like polished gold leaf. Beside him, shoppers moved purposefully through the conveyor belt, their faces etched with determination. Behind them, an unassuming attendant navigated the vast aisle, his eyes darting between shelves and aisles like a skilled detective.

As they waited, a young woman with curly brown hair and warm blue eyes stepped forward. She looked around, her steps light and free. "What can I help you with?" she asked, her voice soft and inviting.

"Nothing," the woman answered, waving her hand dismissively.

"No problem, madam," the attendant replied, extending a helping hand. He scanned the shoppers carefully before settling into his spot. "Take your time. Everything will be done quickly."

As they walked down the long aisle, the lady noticed that some items were missing. A little boy was holding up an empty carton, clearly distraught.

"What happened?" she asked, her tone gentle but stern.

"We misplaced our favorite fruits," the child said tearfully. The attendant nodded silently. "No worries, dear. Just put it back where you found it."

Just then, a shopper approached from behind, clattering her shopping cart onto the counter. He bent down and tapped his knee on a stack of plastic bins.

"Aren't those my apples?" he asked, looking around anxiously.

"They're not ours," the attendant replied, pointing towards a display case.

"Are you sure? Let me check."

With a quick glance at his pocket, he turned to the attendant once again. "We need to get rid of them. This way, please," he commanded, leading the store clerk toward the nearest bin.

The attendant led the way, carrying a large bag and a clipboard filled with receipts. They reached the next section—the bar code scanner—where they clicked their fingers, scanning the contents as eagerly as if they had never seen anything else before.

Inside, the registers buzzed with activity, showing detailed inventory counts. Suddenly, there was a faint beep, indicating that the customer had entered their total amount correctly.

"Thank you," the shopper said, shaking the attendant’s hand.

The attendant returned the item, offering a smile. "It won’t cost you anything," he replied, handing the shopper the receipt.

After their purchases were complete, the shopper thanked the attendant and exited the store. As he moved away, the man behind him leaned against the wall, tears welling up in his eyes.

"You look pretty upset," the woman nearby commented, her face contorting with emotion.

"I'm just happy we didn't lose any more things," the man replied, wiping his brow and turning away.

Suddenly, a loud noise echoed through the crowded room—a sound so sudden and powerful it made everyone pause. There was an immediate rush of motion among the shoppers—men pushing carts, women running, children huddling close together, sounds of frantic laughter and cries.

The attendant glanced nervously around the narrow aisle. "What did we do wrong?"

"Nothing," the woman explained, her voice trembling.

"But what about these other kids? Why did they crowd us?" she asked, her expression questioning yet also understanding.

"The other kids wanted to share too," the woman admitted. "I didn't expect them to."

The shoppers burst into laughter, many laughing loudly enough to break through the thinning ceiling. The man, feeling uneasy, tried to calm them down, but they kept rolling their eyes and groaning in amusement at his attempt.

Finally, the attendant gathered the group of shoppers into one group, trying to soothe their nerves.

"Whoa, aren't we lucky to have such a harmonious group," the woman laughed out loud.

"It might make things easier later when we have more time," the man agreed, rubbing his temples.

As the crowd dispersed and they headed back to their separate areas, the cashier took a deep breath, his face a mask of determination. "Good luck," he muttered to the shopkeeper as he left. "We'll figure this out."

Cara, il cliente stai davanti e sta per comprare un altro cartello. Ora, ecco come la scena è passata. Inizia per cui c'è qualcuno che sta cercando di fare qualche shopping. 

A questo punto, la cosa si fa più difficile perché non ci sono più chiavi disponibili. Di fronte a lui, si intravedono i suoi confronti, una cartella, un divizzo di argilla, un ritmico dell'accettazione. Questi due elementi formano il complesso principale della scenografia.

Circa cinque minuti dopo, le scene si trasformano perciò in quel momento incredibilmente serio, in quello spesso emotivo dei negativi. 

Il client si accorge che il loro cartello è l'argomento di una conversazione, proprio come gli altri. Ecco ora quando l'acquisto sarà fatto. Sotto questa condizione di acquisto, la cena in questione viene messa in chiaro, mentre il client è distratto dalla situazione. 

E così, tutto ciò che si trova in questo modo è lo stesso che avveniva nella realtà: un mercato, il numero di chiave, la prenotazione di carta, la presenza della regolatore. Questi due concetti sembrano essere stati restringiti in modo diverso, ma hanno sempre trovato il riscontro finale. 

Ecco ora le ultime parole che ho in mano. Questi tre elementi formano il semplice complesso principale. Ciò che vi posso dire qui, solo in italiano, è che in queste scene, tutti quelli dietro sono stati modificati per rendere che tutto si senta nel modo più assolutamente vero.
